title: Misleading Gallery: Traps & Fixes
objective: After this lesson you will be able to spot the six classic visualization traps (truncated axes, dual axes, cherry-picked ranges, area distortion, survivorship framing, hidden denominators) and fix each with a before/after pair.
why: Every trap in this gallery ships regularly in real decks — including, statistically, yours. Recognition plus mechanical fixes (zero baselines, indexed comparisons, full windows, per-unit areas, stated denominators) turns honesty from taste into checklist. Self-caught traps with before/after pairs are credibility evidence in the capstone.

blocks.text: Each trap: signature, mechanism, fix. **Truncated axes** (82-vs-85 doubling visually → zero baseline or declared zoom with context). **Dual axes** (manufactured correlation → indexed/paneled). **Cherry-picked ranges** (spike theater → full comparable windows + selection criteria). **Area distortion** (radius-doubled bubbles quadrupling → sqrt scaling or labels). **Survivorship framing** (success stories without denominators → rates with populations). **Hidden denominators** (percentages without n → always paired).

rows: Zero baseline; declared zoom only with context

blocks.text: The **lie factor** (visual effect size ÷ data effect size; honest = 1.0) makes distortion discussable: truncated 82-vs-85 bars score ~10+ (visual doubling of 3.6% gaps). Compute it for suspect charts (effect in pixels vs effect in data) — numbers move designers where adjectives don't. Anything far from 1.0 gets fixed or explicitly justified.

blocks.caption: Quantified distortion: pixels lie louder than data

blocks.title: Score the lie
blocks.note: Run it: expect ~250 for truncated bars vs 1.0 honest — same data, 250x visual lie. Lie factors turn 'misleading' from accusation into arithmetic.

items: Six traps with signatures + mechanical fixes (baselines, indexing, windows, sqrt, denominators, n)
Lie factor quantifies distortion (visual ÷ data effect; ~1.0 honest)
Self-caught before/after pairs are capstone credibility evidence

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice lie factors and interpret both numbers. (b) Audit one of your own past charts (or the course's Ch.5 example) for two traps from the table, with verdicts. (c) Write the fix for the worse finding as a before/after spec (what changes, what stays).
hints: Numbers: ~250 (visual violence) vs 1.0 (honest) — same data, framing decides truth value.
Self-audit honestly: check axes, ranges, denominators on your own work first (the gallery applies inward).
Before/after spec: baseline restored + range extended + n attached (each fix mechanical, verifiable).
exercise.why: Quantification (lie factors), self-application (own work audited first), and specified fixes (before/after mechanics) are the three honesty judgments — each practiced, with pairs preserved as evidence.
exercise.code: // Honesty-audit pattern: trap table sweep + lie factors + before/after pairs.

quiz.q: 82-vs-85 bars, axis from 80. Lie factor ~250. Action?
options: Zero baseline (factor →1.0) or declared zoom with full context — 250× distortion is never emphasis
quiz.explain: Quantified lies demand mechanical fixes: baselines for magnitudes, declared zooms only with context. Drama is not a defense.

quiz.q: '90% success!' with n hidden. Missing + fix?
options: Denominator: pair every rate with n (9/10 vs 900/1000 differ totally); hidden-n rates are claims without evidence
quiz.explain: Rates without denominators conceal evidence weight. Pairing n is non-negotiable honesty infrastructure.

options: Full comparable windows + stated selection criteria — ranges are framing, criteria make them reviewable
quiz.explain: Unexplained ranges cherry-pick by default suspicion. Comparable windows with criteria turn spikes into findings.

summary: Six traps, lie-factor arithmetic, before/after fixes, self-audits preserved. Honesty mechanical, credibility evidenced.
